title: The last cell
concept: Loop, then handle the last cell once more (the fencepost)

steps.say: Pick up the gem on every cell, the last one included.
Pick, then move, while the way is clear.
Which cell still has its gem at the end?
Run it. On the last cell the way isn't clear, so the loop ends before `pick()`.
5 cells, but only 4 moves: the loop runs 4 times.
Handle the last cell once more, after the loop.
Run it. Loop, then once more: every cell is done.
Run the starter to see which cell it misses. Then add `put()` after the loop, not indented.

recap.say: To do something on every cell up to a wall: loop, then do it once more.

plant_to_wall: Look at the 'one cell' world: that cell needs a gem too.
n cells, n − 1 moves. Put in the loop, then once more after it.
edge_gems: Look at the 'one cell' world: its first cell is also its last.
Put on the first cell, walk to the wall, then put only if the cell is still empty.
